Claims 17, 20, 22, and 27 are amended. Claim 19 is deleted. No new matter is added.
Claims 17-18 and 20-39 are pending after the introduction of the above amendments with claims 28-39 being withdrawn.
I. Summary of Examiner Interview

The Examiner is thanked for the informative call on June 20, 2024. The substance of the call related to the objection over the drawings for adding new matter. The Applicant thanks the Examiner for the productive suggestion.
II. Objections of the Drawings
The drawings were objected to for having new matter. Replacement sheets are provided herewith to overcome the objection. No new matter is added.
III. Objection of the Specification
The Specification was objected to minor informalities. The amendment to the specification herewith is believed to overcome the objection. No new matter is added.
IV. Claim Objections
Claims 17 and 22 were objected to for containing various informalities. It is believed the claim amendments filed herewith overcome the objections.
V. Claim Interpretation - 35 USC §112

Applicant notes that the Examiner has interpreted various features of the claims under 35 U.S.C. § 112(f). Applicant does not concede that 35 U.S.C. § 112(f) applies to the features of the claims as filed. Nevertheless, Applicant amends various claims such that 35 U.S.C. § 112(f) does not apply.
VI. Claim Rejections - 35 USC §112

Claim 20 was rejected under 112(a) for lack of written description for the probe tip using any kind of memory to store the probe tip mass. Claim 20 is amended to specify that the elongate probe tip further comprises an EEPROM memory, which has support in the specification as filed at least at page 7, second paragraph. The Applicant request the rejection be withdrawn based on the present claim amendments.
VII. Claim Rejections - 35 USC §103

Claims 17, 18, and 23-27 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 for being unpatentable over U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2009/0171234 to Gurewitsch (hereinafter "Gurewitsch") in view of U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2014/0114193 to Anthony (hereinafter "Anthony") in view of U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2007/0167819 to Osborn (hereinafter "Osborn) in view of U.S. Patent No. 6,045,517 to Williams (hereinafter "Williams") and in view of U.S. Patent No. 6,258,024 to Van Der Weegan (hereinafter "Van Der Weegan").
Claim 19 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 for being unpatentable over Gurewitsch,

Anthony, Osborn, Williams, Van Der Weegan, in view of US Patent Application Publication No. 2003/0164708 Park (hereinafter "Park"). Claim 19 has been cancelled and the limitations incorporated into claim 17, therefore discussion of Park will be related to Claim 17.
Claim 20 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 for being unpatentable over Gurewitsch,
Anthony, Osborn, Williams, Van Der Weegan, in view of US Patent Application Publication No. 2012/0187000 Kahn (hereinafter "Kahn").
Claims 21 and 22 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 for being unpatentable over
Gurewitsch, Anthony, Osborn, Williams, Van Der Weegan, in view of U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2013/0217979 to Blackadar (hereinafter "Blackadar").
Applicant respectfully submits that claims 17, 18, and 23-27 are allowable for at least the following reasons.

Claim 17 has been amended to include the limitation of original Claim 19 and is further limited to exciting the bridge arrangement by bursts of square wave pulses at a frequency of 1 kHz. The Office Action alleges that Park discloses the use of square wave pulses to excite a Wheatstone bridge arrangement. The Applicant respectfully asserts that Park does not disclose
Page 11 of12

that "the bridge can be excited by bursts of square wave pulses at a frequency of 1 kHz", the additional limitations allow for "the detection of the small resistance change of the load cell bridge with both low power requirements and low sensitivity to DC drift", as described in the specification as filed, page 6, last paragraph. Unlike Claim 17, Park describes a device for measuring conductivity in water using square wave bursts in the range 10-20kHz but does not teach of the frequency of pulses nor that the square wave pulses be delivered at frequency of 1 kHz to detect small resistance changes, such as the small resistance changes cervical measurements to detect preterm labor.

The Applicant respectfully contends that one of ordinary skill in the art would not have modified the apparatus as allegedly described by Gurewitsch, Anthony, Osborn, Williams, and Van Der Weegan by using bursts of square wave pulses at a frequency of 1 kHz to excite the bridge arrangement, as allegedly taught by Park for at least the reasons provided above. Thus, the claims are novel and non-obvious over Gurewitsch, Anthony, Osborn, Williams, Van Der Weegan, and Park, alone or in combination, and the rejection should be withdrawn.

Regarding Claims 18 and 20-27, while Applicant does not agree with or concede to this rejection, Applicant notes that it is axiomatic that dependent claims are non-obvious under Section 103 if the independent claims from which they depend are non-obvious. See In re Fine, 837 F.2d 1071, 1076 (Fed. Cir. 1988). Thus, because independent claim 17 is novel and non- obvious, at least for the reasons argued above, it follows that all dependent claims are non- obvious and in condition for allowance as well.
VIII. Double Patenting

The claims have been provisionally rejected on the grounds of nonstatutory double patenting as being unpatentable over claims 1-9 of U.S. Patent No. 11,660,046 Anumba (hereinafter "Anumba") in view of Gurewitsch, Anthony, Osborn, Williams, Van Der Weegan, Park, Kahn, Blackadar as outlined previously. The applicant respectfully requests the grounds of rejection be deferred until all other matters of substance have been resolved.
